tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the project overview to learn that Paperplane converts PDFs and document images into auditable Markdown and structured JSON. It establishes the OpenAI vision, PyMuPDF, backend, and frontend vocabulary used by the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Architecture Map
tour.description: The architecture guide frames the backend, frontend, persistence, and processing boundaries before following a request through them. Use it as the map for the focused code stops that follow.

tour.title: FastAPI Bootstrap
tour.description: The FastAPI entry point assembles lifecycle services, middleware, routers, and health endpoints. Its settings module shows how runtime configuration controls providers, storage, queues, and telemetry.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI applications compose request handling through routers and middleware, while Pydantic-backed settings validate runtime configuration at startup.

tour.title: Job API Surface
tour.description: These routers expose document job creation, inspection, and V2 job operations to callers. They are the boundary between HTTP requests and the service layer explored next.

tour.title: Persistence and Migrations
tour.description: Database models define the durable records for parsing work, while the database module initializes and manages persistence. Alembic migrations evolve that state over time so the service layer has stable storage contracts.
tour.languageLesson: SQLAlchemy models keep application entities explicit, and ordered Alembic migrations let the schema change alongside code without rebuilding production data.

tour.title: Parsing Contracts
tour.description: The parsing contracts define the immutable layout, region, and stitching vocabulary shared across recognition stages. Reading these first makes the larger V2 pipeline easier to follow because its inputs and outputs are named here.

tour.title: V2 Parsing Pipeline
tour.description: The V2 pipeline performs page-oriented document parsing and reconciles results into the grounded output model. It is the central transformation path behind the API requests introduced in Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses and typed contracts make pipeline stages communicate through explicit structures rather than loosely shaped dictionaries.

tour.title: Job Execution
tour.description: The job queue and worker turn parsing requests into managed background work, including task execution and coordination. This separates durable job lifecycle concerns from the page-processing logic in the pipeline.

tour.title: Frontend Workspace
tour.description: The Next.js page is the main document-processing workspace, coordinating uploads, job polling, controls, and tabs. The root layout supplies the page-level structure and global styling for that user-facing workflow.
tour.languageLesson: React components model the UI as composable state-driven views; Next.js app files provide the page and layout conventions around them.

tour.title: Quality Gates
tour.description: The V2 API tests exercise the request-facing behavior introduced in Step 4, while the quality guide explains the evaluation policy around extraction results. Together they show how changes are checked at both functional and output-quality levels.

tour.title: Packaging and Delivery
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the backend into a minimal non-root runtime image, and Compose supplies the local multi-service topology. The CI workflow then runs linting, typing, tests, documentation checks, packaging validation, and frontend checks on main changes.
tour.languageLesson: Docker multi-stage builds separate dependency installation from the runtime image, while GitHub Actions organizes automated checks into triggered jobs and steps.
